label: This month
why: The 30 days before this cache was made. Shown in the game as cached, never as live.
source: NASA DONKI (Space Weather Database Of Notifications, Knowledge, Information)
note: Cached copy. Fields trimmed for size; each record links to its full DONKI page.

CME.note: CME seen to the ESE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source may be some minor field line movement beyond the ESE limb in SDO AIA 171 beginning as early as 2026-10-15T18:00Z.

Faint, wide CME visible to the SW in STEREO A COR2 only. The CME is not clearly seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The potential source is not clearly visible. There is a data gap in STEREO A COR2 and EUV imagery in real-time from 2026-10-15T12:09Z to 2026-10-16T06:09Z. A potential source may be seen in STEREO A EUV imagery anywhere from longitudes W90 to approximately W120 as a gradual, minor dimming may be seen after the data gap starting around 2026-10-16T06:09Z. However, there are not strong post-eruption signatures in imagery, and there is low confidence in this analysis of the source location.
Narrow CME visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery. No source is found for this CME in EUV imagery.

CME faintly visible to the NNW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2. The source for this CME is not found in available EUV imagery, and the CME may be farsided.

CME visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely beyond the east limb, as moving/opening field lines are seen in SDO AIA 171 in ISWA as early as 2026-10-16T10:28Z.

CME visible faintly to the NE in STEREO A COR2. The CME is not seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The potential source is an eruption starting around 2026-10-16T11:00Z, primarily centered around N05E10, although the eruption extends as far east as N05E30. The eruption may include a filament liftoff as seen in SDO AIA 304. Dimming, moving/opening field lines, and post-eruptive arcades are best seen in SDO AIA 193. The eruption is also seen near the NE limb from the point of view of STEREO A EUV 195 and 304 imagery. This CME may exhibit deflection due to its proximity to the coronal hole.

Bright CME seen to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and to the NW in STEREO A COR2. Its source is likely a messy eruption seen in the NW quadrant in STEREO A EUV 195/304 and centered very approximately around N12W140 near former Active Region 14549 starting 2026-10-16T14:25Z. Coronal signatures include dimming, post-eruptive arcades and ejecta seen in STEREO A EUV 195/304, as well as opening/moving of field lines behind the NW limb in SDO AIA 193/171.

Faint and narrow CME seen to the E in early SOHO LASCO C2 imagery and not seen in C3, GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2 imagery, likely because of its faintness. The start time is likely at least an hour earlier but the CME becomes clear around 17Z. No clear source found, so the CME is likely far sided.

Narrow very minor CME/outflow visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The start of the CME/outflow is likely much earlier. No source is found for this CME in EUV imagery.

CME first seen to the ESE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-10-17T02:48Z. It is also seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C3. The CME is also seen later in its propagation to the E GOES CCOR-1 near the edge of the  FOV as the early frames of the CME are obscured by Earthshine. It is also seen to the SE in STEREO A COR2 as a partial halo. The leading edge of the CME is somewhat irregularly shared with the nose farther to the south. The source is a filament eruption on or slightly beyond the SE limb best seen in SDO AIA 304 beginning around 2026-10-17T01:00Z. A wide opening of field lines can also been seen in SDO AIA 171 and SDO AIA 193.

Narrow CME/outflow to the E seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The CME is not seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery, which is available. No clear source was found in EUV imagery, so the CME is possibly far-sided.
Narrow CME/outflow to the E seen in SOHO LASCO C2. The CME is not seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery. This CME/outflow is following the 2026-10-17T17:00Z CME. No clear source was found in EUV imagery.

Faint CME first seen to the NW by GOES CCOR-1 beginning at 2026-10-18T21:30Z. This CME is not visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or STEREO A COR2 in real time due to data gaps beginning at 2026-10-18T19:12Z and 2026-10-18T20:38Z respectively. The source of this event is a small region of dimming and field line opening seen in the vicinity of N10W30, extending Northward, in SDO AIA 193 beginning at approx. 2026-10-18T19:00Z.

CME first seen to the West by GOES CCOR-1 beginning at 2026-10-18T23:15Z. This CME is not visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or STEREO A COR2 in real time due to data gaps beginning at 2026-10-18T19:12Z and 2026-10-18T20:38Z respectively. The source of this event is field line opening seen on/beyond the West limb in GOES SUVI 284 beginning at approx. 2026-10-18T19:30Z.

CME first seen to the NNW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-10-19T14:48Z. This CME is also seen to the NNW in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the NW in STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is an eruption beyond the NW limb seen as moving field lines beyond the NW limb in STEREO A EUVI 195 beginning around 2026-10-19T11:05Z. The eruption likely occurred in proximity to a large coronal hole that is approaching the western limb from the perspective of STEREO A. Some deflection is likely.

Faint CME observed to the NW in GOES CCOR-1. It may be visible to the NW in STEREO A COR2, but only one available frame of imagery does not clearly show the CME. No real-time visibility in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 due to a data gap starting around 2026-10-19T18:48Z. The source is likely far-sided from Earth, observed around N10W130 as brightening in STEREO A EUVI 304 at 2026-10-19T18:15Z, and EUVI 195 at 2026-10-19T18:25Z. Also observed over the NW limb in GOES SUVI 284 as faint field line movement.

CME first seen to the NNW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-10-20T01:26Z. It is also seen to the NNW in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the NW in STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is most likely far-sided due to a lack of source candidates on the Earth-facing disk. Some very faint field line movement beyond the N limb in GOES SUVI 284 that may be related is visible beginning around 2026-10-19T23:00Z. A far-sided source is consistent with triangulated measurements.

Narrow CME first seen to the NNW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-10-20T07:24Z. It is also seen to the NNW in SOHO LASCO C3 and to the NW in STEREO A COR2 but is too diffuse to reliably track in GOES CCOR-1. There are no source candidates on the Earth-facing disk, so the source is most likely far-sided. A far-sided source is consistent with triangulated measurements.

CME first seem to the NW in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-10-20T09:09Z. It is also seen to the NNW in SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1 but is covered by a real-time data gap in SOHO LASCO C3. The source of this CME is most likely far-sided due to a lack of source candidates. A far-sided source is consistent with triangulated measurements.

Narrow CME first seen to the NW in STEREO A COR2 starting around 2026-10-20T14:23Z. It is also seen to the NNW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. There are no source candidates on the Earth-facing disk, so the source is most likely far-sided. A far-sided source is consistent with triangulated measurements.

CME first seen to the East by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-10-21T08:53Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is a small eruption seen centered at approx. N40E05 beginning at approx. 2026-10-21T08:15Z as seen in SDO AIA 193. Dimming signatures extending to the Southeast (approx. N20E25) seen in SDO AIA 193 and proximity to a small coronal hole indicate a potential strong SE deflection of this event.

CME first seen to the NW by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-10-21T13:38Z, as well as to the North in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this CME is likely far sided, and can be seen as field line opening from beyond the West limb in STEREO A EUVI 195 imagery beginning at approx. 2026-10-21T13:05Z.

CME observed to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and to the NW in STEREO A COR2. The source is likely far-sided and may not be observed, with the only potential observation in GOES SUVI 284 starting ~2026-10-21T20:14Z as field line movement on/near the N limb; however faint high northern latitude on-disk brightening near this time in GOES SUVI 284 indicates that motion may trace on-disk and not to the far-side. In STEREO A EUVI 195/304, a change in field lines and prominence material can be seen on the west limb after a lengthy data gap ends spanning approximately 2026-10-21T15:15Z to 2026-10-21T20:45Z, and may indicate the source without directly observing the eruption. Based on the current estimated location of former Active Regions 14545 and 14549 around E150-E170 and the triangulated analysis, those former regions may be the source for this event.

Thin CME observed to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not observed in STEREO A COR2 with a data gap starting at 2026-10-22T17:23Z. The source is likely far-sided, only potentially visible as faint field line motion over the N limb in GOES SUVI 284 around 2026-10-22T19:18Z.

Faint CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not observed in STEREO A COR2 due to a real time data gap spanning 2026-10-22T17:53Z to 2026-10-23T01:23Z, where it may be too faint to observe afterwards. No distinct source is observed on disk and may be far-sided, with weak field line movement over the NE limb as early as 2026-10-22T20:00Z in SDO AIA 171 noted as a potential, weak candidate.

This CME is visible to the northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and to the north in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is a C1.3 flare and eruption from Active Region 14557 (centered near N10W90) starting around 2026-10-23T03:45Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. An opening of field lines is visible over the northwest limb in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284 imagery at this time as well.

This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. Despite data availability during this time, this event is likely far-sided from the perspective of STEREO A and is therefore not observed by STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.
A super faint CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and not seen in STEREO A COR2. No source seen in EUV imagery, so this outflow is possibly far-sided.

Narrow CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-10-24T15:12Z. It is also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the N in STEREO A COR2. The source is likely related to field line movement seen beyond the NE in in SDO AIA 193 starting around 2026-10-24T14:42Z.

A very minor CME to the E only seen in GOES CCOR-1 and not seen in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph; the CME is covered by the unfilled scheduled data gap in SOHO LASCO coronagraph. No source has been seen in EUV imagery for this CME.

CME observed to the SW in STEREO A COR and GOES CCOR-1, not observed in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 due to a data gap from approximately 2026-10-24T16:48Z - 2026-10-24T20:36Z. No source is observed in available EUV imagery, including STEREO A EUVI, and is likely far-sided.
A narrow jet-like CME seen to the WSW in all three coronagraphs. No source has been found for this jet-like feature in the EUV imagery.

Relatively narrow CME to the NNW seen in SOHO LASCO C2 and in GOES CCOR-1. This CME is not seen in SOHO LASCO C3 because of poor image quality. It is covered by the data gap in STEREO A COR2 so far. The source is likely the opening/movement of field lines and possibly small ejecta seen on/beyond the NW limb in SDO AIA 193/171/131/304 after 2026-10-24T21:12Z.

Faint CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is far-sided, observed in GOES SUVI 284 as field line movement beyond the W limb around 2026-10-24T22:06Z, and may be directly observed in STEREO A EUVI 304 as brightening in the vicinity of former AR 14551 at 2026-10-24T20:45Z.

CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and faintly to the N in STEREO A COR2. The source is wide field line movement over the E limb starting around 2026-10-25T02:09Z in SDO AIA 171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284/304; the prominence on the limb jostles in SDO AIA 304/GOES SUVI 304  but does not cleanly erupt. Preceeded by and overtakes a faint leading edge starting at 2026-10-25T01:48Z measuring ~173 km/s, from field line movement over the NE limb ~2026-10-25T00:58Z in GOES SUVI 284 prior to the main eruption. Followed by and overlaps with a streamer blowout starting around 2026-10-25T05:00Z.

CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, starting very slow. It is either not yet seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap beginning at 2026-10-25T10:09Z or too faint to resolve the leading edge. The source appears to be a mix of continued slow field line movement over the E limb following CME 2026-10-25T03:12Z, whose eruption began around 2026-10-25T02:09Z in SDO AIA 171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284/304, and/or further field line movement in GOES SUVI 171/284 starting around 2026-10-25T04:30Z.

Faint CME observed to the N in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. It is likely not observed in STEREO A COR2, but the NW quadrant of COR2 imagery is overlapped with prior CME activity and may obscure this front. The source is likely far-sided, due to the lack of any on-disk EUV observations corresponding to this front time.

CME first seen to the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-10-25T19:24Z. The source of this event is a small filament eruption seen in SDO AIA 304 located at approx. S10W60, beginning at approx. 2026-10-25T18:42Z. Field line opening is also seen in SDO AIA 171/193.

Faint CME observed to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not observed in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap. The source is likely far-sided over the east limb, potentially observed as field line movement in GOES SUVI 284 around 2026-10-25T23:06Z.

This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 in real time due to a data gap. The source may be related to an opening of field lines visible over the western limb in SDO AIA 171 imagery starting around 2026-10-25T23:55Z, likely associated with a small eruption from Active Region 14560 (N14W75).

This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. There is a data gap in STEREO A COR2 imagery at the time of this CME. The source may be related to a small eruption from Active Region 14560 (N14W75) seen best in SDO AIA 131/193/304 imagery starting around 2026-10-26T01:30Z.

CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the SE in STEREO A COR2. This CME precedes and is partially overlapped by the larger CME: 2026-10-26T09:48Z, very likely from the same source. The source is newly developed AR 14561, with two distinct but close proximity eruptive signatures, likely responsible for this leading edge and CME: 2026-10-26T09:48Z. For this leading edge, the eruptive source is likely field line movement/brightening in SDO AIA 171/193, and on-disk brightening in SDO AIA 304 and STEREO A EUVI 304, starting around 2026-10-26T08:31Z and centered around S09W72. This eruption is also associated with a C1.9 flare peaking at 2026-10-26T08:38Z, observed in SDO AIA 131.

CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the SE in STEREO A COR2. This CME follows the more faint CME: 2026-10-26T09:00Z, very likely from the same source. The source is newly developed AR 14561, with two distinct but close proximity eruptive signatures, likely responsible for this front and CME: 2026-10-26T09:00Z. For this CME, the eruptive source is likely an area of dimming and field line movement centered ~S05W80 in the vicinity of AR 14561, observed in SDO AIA 171/195, GOES SUVI 284, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304, starting around 2026-10-26T09:10Z. This follows separate field line movement/brightening in SDO AIA 171/193 starting around 2026-10-26T08:31Z ~S09W72, likely responsible for preceding CME: 2026-10-26T09:00Z.

This CME is visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. This event is not visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery despite data availability, likely because it is directed towards the spacecraft and therefore occulted by the coronagraph. The source is related to an eruption and C2.8 flare from Active Region 14561 (S12W77) starting around 2026-10-26T18:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. A subsequent opening of field lines is visible over the southwest limb as seen in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284 imagery.

This CME is visible to the northeast in SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery.  This event was also seen in SOHO LASCO C3 after a downlink data gap backfilled and was seen in STEREO A COR2 after a data gap from 2026-10-26T20:38Z to 2026-10-27T02:23Z. The source is a large filament eruption visible near the eastern limb which begins to lift off around 2026-10-26T20:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 171/193/304 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284/304 imagery. The filament may extend as far as longitude E50 to beyond the east limb. A subsequent opening of field lines is visible over the northeast limb in GOES SUVI 284 imagery.

Narrow CME visible to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and the NE in STEREO A COR2. The potential source may be a faint filament eruption best seen starting around 2026-10-27T02:16Z in GOES SUVI 304 imagery. Post-eruption dimming can also be seen in SDO AIA 193 centered around N40E20.
Faint CME visible to the NE in STEREO A COR2. The CME is not clearly visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The potential source location is not found in available EUV imagery.

Faint CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source may be field line movement on/near the high latitude N limb around 2026-10-27T22:31Z in SDO AIA 171, or far-sided and unobserved.

Faint CME observed to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, also very faintly observed to the SW in STEREO A COR2, becoming more defined as it travels further into each coronagraph's field-of-view. The source is likely former AR 14561, located around S10W95 at this time. There is no distinct, clean eruption associated with this CME, but rather slow field line movement and brightening from this region of the disk in GOES SUVI 284 starting around 2026-10-28T09:46Z, also observed as some field line movement and brightening near AR 14561 in STEREO A EUVI 195.

This CME is visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the east in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is a filament eruption with liftoff starting around 2026-10-29T07:36Z seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. The footpoints extend from about S20W20 to S10W50. Post eruptive dimming is visible in SDO AIA 193 with an opening of field lines seen over the southwest limb in SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 171/284 imagery.

Very minor and faint CME seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and in GOES CCOR-1 coronagraphs. This CME is not seen in STEREO A COR2. Its source is a very minor eruption from the former AR 14561 (S10W130) starting ~2026-10-30T11:25Z as seen in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery. AR 14561 rotated off of the Earth-facing disk on 2026-10-27.

CME first seen to the West by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-10-31T05:00Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME is not clearly seen in STEREO A COR2, as it may be obscured by the pylon or too faint to view clearly. The source of this event is an eruption from former AR 14561 (S11W140) beginning at approx. 2026-10-31T04:30Z as seen in STEREO A EUVI 195. Brightening near the region and dimming extending Northward can be seen in association with this eruption, possibly suggesting a Northern deflection.

Diffuse CME first seen to the SE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-11-01T00:00Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is a small filament eruption seen centered at approx. S15E65 beginning at approx. 2026-10-31T23:25Z as seen in SDO AIA 304. Post eruptive arcades and field line movement is also visible in SDO AIA 171/193. This eruption is in close proximity to a coronal hole, potentially resulting in some deflection.

CME first seen to the West in SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-11-01T19:00Z. The CME is also visible to the west in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The CME may be faintly visible to the east in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source of this event is a filament eruption seen centered at approx. N15W15. Filament destabilization began at approx. 2026-11-01T16:43Z, with liftoff beginning at approx. 2026-11-01T17:54Z as seen in SDO AIA, STEREO A EUVI and GOES SUVI 304. Post eruptive arcades and field line movement are also visible in SDO AIA 193, GOES SUVI 284 and STEREO A EUVI 195.

Slow developing CME first seen to the NE by SOHO LASCO C2, also observed in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not observed in STEREO A COR due to a data gap in real-time starting at 2026-11-01T19:38Z. The source of this event is an eruption from beyond the NE limb seen in GOES SUVI 284/304 beginning at approx. 2026-11-01T18:14Z as filament ejecta and very wide, slow field line movement. An initial faint CME at 2026-11-01T18:36Z (LASCO C2) measuring plane-of-sky ~164 km/s is observed prior to this brighter emerging front.

Wide, slow CME observed to the E in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap beginning at 2026-11-03T18:36Z. This CME is very slow to erupt, speeding up well after its first observation in SOHO LASCO C2. The source is observed in GOES SUVI 171/195/284 starting loosely around 2026-11-03T08:00Z as wide, slow field line movement lasting several hours on/near the E limb, and source may be slightly far-sided.

Faint CME first seen to the NW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-11-04T02:48Z. This CME fades before exiting the field-of-view in SOHO LASCO C2, and is therefore not visible in GOES CCOR-1 or SOHO LASCO C3. This CME and source are also obscured by a data gap in STEREO A COR2 from 2026-11-03T18:23Z to 2026-11-04T04:23Z. The source of this event is field line movement seen beyond the NW limb beginning at approx. 2026-11-04T02:00Z as seen in SOD AIA 171.

CME faintly visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source is unclear, but may be a small eruption seen near the northeast limb in GOES SUVI 304 as an ejecta of material starting around 2026-11-05T03:24Z.
CME faintly visible to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The CME is not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1 or STEREO A COR2 imagery. There is no clear source for this CME seen in available EUV imagery.

CME first seen in white light imagery to the E in GOES CCOR-1 starting at 2026-11-05T20:00Z. In real time, this CME is covered by data gaps in SOHO LASCO and STEREO A COR2. The source of this CME is like related to an M3.5 class flare from AR 14566 (S08E35) which peaked at 2026-11-05T18:33Z. The flare is best seen in SDO AIA 131. Some post-eruptive dimming can also be seen in SDO AIA 193. Due to the source location being in close proximity to a coronal hole, some deflection is likely.

CME seen to the east in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is also faintly visible to the east in STEREO A COR2 after a data gap from 2026-11-05T14:35Z to 2026-11-06T01:38Z. The potential source location may be a minor eruption seen near the SE limb in GOES SUVI 304 imagery starting around 2026-11-05T19:28Z located near S15E75. Moving/opening field lines are also best seen in SDO AIA 171/193 imagery.

Narrow CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source may possibly be a minor eruption starting around 2026-11-06T00:22Z in as best seen in SDO AIA 193, with moving field lines seen around S15E70.

Narrow CME visible to the west in STEREO A COR2. The CME is not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery is not available due to a downlink data gap. The potential source is an eruption seen near the west limb in STEREO A EUV 195/304 located around N20W160 starting around 2026-11-06T03:15Z. The eruption can be seen as an ejecta of material in STEREO A EUV 304. Moving field lines and post-eruption arcades are also visible in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery.

CME visible to the NE in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME may also be faintly visible to the NNE in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The start of the CME may be faintly visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2  at the time of the analysis, but was not visible in SOHO LASCO C3 in real time due to a downlink data gap. The source is an eruption just on or beyond the NE limb as seen in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284 imagery seen as opening field lines starting at 2026-11-06T06:16Z.

Wide CME visible to the NW in GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. The CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery in real-time due to a data gap starting at 2026-11-06T13:38Z. The likely source is a filament eruption that starts to lift off in STEREO A EUV 304 imagery, around N35W140, starting at 2026-11-06T13:15Z. The filament can also be seen lifting off beyond the west limb in GOES SUVI 304 imagery.  Moving/opening field lines are also visible in SDO AIA 171 in ISWA, SDO AIA 193, and GOES SUVI 284 imagery.

A very minor CME see to the NW in LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. This CME is not seen STEREO A COR2 as there is a data gap. It is possible that this CME is an outflow following the 2026-11-06T16:15Z CME. No clear source for this CME has been found.

Faint CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source is likely field line movement on/near the high latitude NE limb, observed starting around 2026-11-07T03:55Z in SDO AIA 171.

First in a pair of far-sided CMEs from a filament eruption, followed by slower CME 2026-11-07T10:24Z.  This leading edge is more faint and observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source for both is a far-sided filament eruption, observed well in GOES SUVI 284/304 over the N limb starting around 2026-11-07T08:04Z, with the filament first lifting off as early as 2026-11-07T06:51Z. Also observed to the NW in STEREO A EUVI 195 as field line movement around 2026-11-07T08:35Z and STEREO A EUVI 304 as filament ejecta around 2026-11-07T06:15Z.

Second in a pair of far-sided CMEs from a filament eruption, following faster CME 2026-11-07T09:36Z.  This leading edge is brighter and observed to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the NW in STEREO A COR2. The source for both is a far-sided filament eruption, observed well in GOES SUVI 284/304 over the N limb starting around 2026-11-07T08:04Z, with the filament first lifting off as early as 2026-11-07T06:51Z. Also observed to the NW in STEREO A EUVI 195 as field line movement around 2026-11-07T08:35Z and STEREO A EUVI 304 as filament ejecta around 2026-11-07T06:15Z. This second CME is likely delayed filament material following the main eruption, observed deflecting eastward in GOES SUVI 304 and exiting the field-of-view by 2026-11-07T12:24Z.

CME visible to the NW in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME may also be faintly visible in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery prior to a data gap starting at 2026-11-07T21:12Z. The CME is not clearly visible in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source may be a filament eruption seen beyond the NW limb from the point of view of STEREO A EUV 304 imagery starting at 2026-11-07T15:45Z. The eruption can also be seen beyond the NW limb from the point of view of GOES SUVI 304 imagery.
Faint CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. No source is observed in EUV imagery and is likely far-sided.

Faint CME observed to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The source may be further far-sided or observed as field line movement on the W limb in GOES SUVI 195/284 starting around 2026-11-08T05:00Z.

Faint CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2, and faintly in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not observed in STEREO A COR2. The source may be faint field line movement on or slightly beyond the NE limb in GOES SUVI 171 around 2026-11-09T07:06Z. This front is followed by a faint, slow, wide structure measuring approximately 122 km/s plane-of-sky, which may also be related to this eruption or separate far-sided, without current STEREO A COR2 to help differentiate.

Faint CME observed to the W only in STEREO A COR2 before a data gap begins at 2026-11-09T11:38Z, or in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 at all. No source is observed for this CME in available imagery.

Faint, narrow CME observed to the W only in GOES CCOR-1, due to a real-time data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2. The source is likely an eruption from AR 14571 starting around 2026-11-09T15:57Z, observed as dimming and brightening in SDO AIA 193 and field line movement in SDO AIA 171.
Thin, faint CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1, very faint in LASCO C2 and not observed in available STEREO A COR2 imagery. No distinct source is observed for this front.

Wide, diffuse CME observed to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. No distinct source observation or timing is observed beyond broad, slow, near-background movement of field lines in the SE quadrant of GOES SUVI 284 starting as early as 2026-11-10T17:00Z well before the first CME observation in SOHO LASCO C2.

Thin, faint CME observed to the W in GOES CCOR-1 (partially obscured by earthshine) and STEREO A COR2, also in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 after a data gap spanning approx. 2026-11-10T03:00Z - 2026-11-10T07:24Z. The source is AR 14571, with field line movement, brightening, and some small filament ejecta in SDO AIA 171/193/304 starting around 2026-11-10T03:56Z and centered ~S17W72.

CME first seen to the NW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-11-11T23:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME is not visible in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap which began at 2026-11-11T12:23Z. The source of this event is field line opening seen originating from Active Region 14565 (N14W86) in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 284 beginning at approx. 2026-11-11T22:55Z. This AR is in close proximity to a large coronal hole, potentially resulting in some deflection.

CME first seen to the W part way into the FOV of STEREO A COR2 following a real-time data gap that ended at 2026-11-12T01:53Z. The source may be related to some "flickering" seen beyond the WSW limb in STA EUVI after a real-time data gap ending at 2026-11-12T01:55Z.

Faint CME seen to NNW in early SOHO LASCO C2 coronagraph imagery and very faintly in early timestamps of GOES CCOR-1 but completely covered by an evening data gap in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph. Its source is most likely a faint prominence seen erupting on/behind the NNW limb starting at 2026-11-12T21:13Z, as seen to the NNW in GOES SUVI 304. Unfortunately, the source cannot be seen in STEREO A EUV imagery, since it is covered by the above mentioned data gap in STEREO A.

CME visible to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery and to the SSE in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The potential source is not clear, but some faint dimming and moving field lines are seen to the far south in SDO AIA 171/193 imagery starting around 2026-11-12T17:30Z.

This CME is faintly visible to the NE in STEREO A COR2 and SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The CME is not seen in GOES CCOR-1 due to Earthshine starting 2026-11-13T03:45Z. The potential source may be an eruption with a small region of dimming and post-eruption arcades starting at 2026-11-13T00:21Z as best seen in SDO AIA 193 imagery from Active Region 14575 (S09E50).

CME faintly visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is not clear, but may be some faint field line movement seen to the west in STEREO A COR2 EUV 195 imagery around 2026-11-13T08:00Z. Dimming is also seen to the south of the large coronal hole seen in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery as well. Moving/opening field lines are visible beyond the west limb in SDO AIA 171 in ISWA starting at 2026-11-13T08:27Z.

A faint messy front seen to the SSW in SOHO LASCO C2 and later in C3 and GOES CCOR-1 as a messy fuzzy half-loop. There is also a much fainter loop seen in STEREO A COR2 coronagraph to the SW, but this loop in STEREO A COR2 seems to be starting much earlier (first seen ~13Z), so it is likely a different event.

A very small CME seen to the SSW in SOHO LASCO C2 and to the SE in STEREO A COR2 coronagraphs, and in early timestamps of C3. The front is not clear in GOES CCOR-1. No source has been found for this CME.
